clue.text: Our codes are refined and proper

indicators.note: refined here means processed and reworked, so the letters of our codes are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast that one's ethical codes are polished and correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refined' looks like part of the definition beside 'proper', but it is the signal to rearrange OUR CODES; 'are' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorous behaviour is seemly, polite and in keeping with good taste.

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words rude barmaid

explanation.surface: A pub-goer is barred after being insulted by a rude barmaid.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar someone is to exclude them, shutting them out of a place.

clue.text: One may still carry a torch for them

definitions.text: One may still carry a torch for them

parts.words: One may still carry a torch for them
parts.note: to carry a torch for someone is to keep loving them after the affair has ended; the torch suggests a flame

explanation.surface: Someone nursing unrequited feelings for past partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Former sweethearts are the people one might still pine for long after breaking up.

clue.text: Gets stain out after smell returns

indicators.note: after places the rearranged stain behind the turned smell
returns means the abbreviation for smell is read backwards

parts.note: BO is body odour, a smell

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of stain are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cleaner succeeds in shifting a stain once a bad odour comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns BO into OB, and 'out' rearranges STAIN into TAINS, which 'after' puts behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain something is to acquire it; gets is a plain synonym.

parts.note: unions sound like trade unions reacting to job losses, but they are marriages forced by the threat of a gun being fired

explanation.surface: Trade unions taking action over threatened redundancies.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced marriage, traditionally made at gunpoint by the bride's father, is a marriage made under the threat of being shot.

indicators.note: outside says the word for sleeps sits around the word for mother

parts.note: to nod is to doze off, so sleeps gives nods
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother of no fixed abode bedding down in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like where she sleeps, but it puts NODS around MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderers who move from place to place, with no settled home, are people without a fixed dwelling.

clue.text: Put down a score for a round, perhaps

definitions.text: Put down a score for a round, perhaps

parts.words: Put down a score for a round, perhaps
parts.note: suggests recording a golf score for one round, but means writing out music for a round, the kind of song sung in canon

explanation.surface: A golfer writing their total on the card after eighteen holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Written in musical symbols: a composer writes the parts of a canon-like song on the stave.

clue.text: Is it possible for me to be friendly?

definitions.text: Is it possible for me to be

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether they can manage to be pleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as AM I ABLE, the first part asks whether the speaker can do something; the whole is an ordinary adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Read in three words it asks whether the speaker can do something; as one word it means good-natured and agreeable.

parts.note: something easy is simple
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that pointing something out is easy, you fool.
explanation.walkthrough: N is a compass point, a common crossword abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A simpleton is a foolish or gullible person, a fool.

indicators.note: said tells us the word for outlawed is only heard, so a soundalike is written

parts.note: something outlawed is banned
it is taken as written, its apostrophe s a link

explanation.surface: A remark that the outlaw has been prohibited, so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'banned it' and you hear the answer; the 's of 'Outlaw's' is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is a robber living outside the law, a brigand.

clue.text: Hope work's part-time and is minute

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: part says only a portion of the word time is used, its first three letters

explanation.surface: Someone hoping their job is part-time and tiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part-time' is read as 'part' of 'time', giving TIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimism is a hopeful, confident outlook on the future.

indicators.note: in places the word for partner inside the word for group

parts.note: a ring is a group, as of conspirators
an ally is a partner

explanation.surface: A dance partner joins a circle as the group re-forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallying troops or supporters are gathering together again after a setback.

indicators.note: the constituents of something are its parts, here the letters of T Blair rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair's voters are said to be a closed little group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' suggests the voters in a former Prime Minister's seat, but it rearranges T BLAIR; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal loyalties are fiercely partisan, favouring one's own narrow group.

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters of rap means are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unfair accusation brings bad luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard cheese' is British slang for bad luck, which suits the surface, but here it is literal: a hard Italian cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian cheese is hard and grainy, usually grated over pasta.

clue.text: The man at the top's a quiet lodger

parts.note: P, piano, is the music abbreviation for quiet
a lodger is a resident in someone's house

explanation.surface: The head of the household turns out to be a quiet lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'top's' stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state or organisation.

clue.text: Desert storm with England's leader replaced by Iraq's. Most ironic!

indicators.note: storm suggests turmoil, so the letters of desert are thrown into a new order
replaced by says one letter is swapped out for another
the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the leading letter of England is E
taking leader from before, Iraq's leader is I

explanation.surface: Operation Desert Storm, with Britain's leader swapped for Iraq's: ironic.
explanation.walkthrough: One E of DESERT is swapped for I ('leader' serves both countries), giving DISERT, which 'storm' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry humour is wry and understated, so the driest wit is the most sardonic.

clue.text: Without a will of one's own

definitions.text: Without a will of one's own

parts.words: Without a will of one's own
parts.note: suggests someone weak-willed, but means dying having made no will

explanation.surface: A spineless person with no determination.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies without having made a legal testament leaves an estate passed on by law.

clue.text: He made light of his inspiration and…

definitions.text: He made light of his inspiration and…

parts.words: He made light of his inspiration and…
parts.note: made light of sounds like shrugging off, but means an inventor who made the electric light bulb from his idea

explanation.surface: Someone who dismissed his own bright idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 18 across, another famous inspired man.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Alva Edison, the American inventor, developed a practical incandescent light bulb.

parts.note: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French painter
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: The way into an artists' district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'quarter' means a compass point, not a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is the act or means of entering, a way in.

explanation.surface: A fruitcake standing in for someone odder.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruitcake is full of nuts, so more nut-filled; and a fruitcake is also slang for an eccentric, so crazier.

parts.note: relatively seems to mean fairly, but points to the physicist famous for the theory of relativity

explanation.surface: A man who was moderately creative.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein, the German-born physicist, formulated the theories of special and general relativity.

clue.text: A source of inspiration under the bridge

definitions.text: A source of inspiration under the bridge

parts.words: A source of inspiration under the bridge
parts.note: inspiration here is breathing in, and the bridge is the bony top of the nose

explanation.surface: An artist finding ideas beneath a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Air is breathed in through these openings, which sit beneath the ridge of the nose.

clue.text: Take in — for a laugh, say

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and a soundalike is written

parts.note: doing something for a laugh is doing it in jest

explanation.surface: Someone swallowed a story just for fun.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to swallow food or drink into the body.

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name, with the possessive s
an aster is a flower, something that blooms

explanation.surface: A girl's blunder leads to a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bloomer' is British slang for a blunder, which fits the surface; here it is a plant that blooms. 'produces' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity, a catastrophic mishap.

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the cherry tree is flowering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blooming' and the answer are both mild British swear words, as in 'blooming nuisance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry and the answer both name a reddish colour; blooming and the answer are both mild intensifying oaths.

indicators.note: fiddling means tampering, so the letters of Nero and exit are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nero fiddled while Rome burned, then left the stage under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero is said to have fiddled while Rome burned, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Exertion is great physical or mental effort, a strenuous push.

parts.note: suggests yelling proudly, but a pride is a group of lions, which do this loudly

explanation.surface: A proud parent yelling at a school sports day.
explanation.definitionFit: Lions in a pride make a deep, loud cry, and a person who bellowed did the same.

clue.text: He may try a bit of duck taken from grill

indicators.note: taken from says the letter for duck is removed from the word for grill

parts.note: a toaster is a grill for bread
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, so O

explanation.surface: A chef sampling a morsel of duck taken off the grill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of duck' reads together, but 'a bit' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is someone who samples food or drink to judge it.

clue.text: Having enough money for crack cocaine in new York

parts.note: to crack a puzzle is to solve it

indicators.note: in places the letter for cocaine inside the letters for new York

parts.note: Y is short for York, as in NY
C is slang for cocaine

explanation.surface: Funds enough to buy crack cocaine in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' and 'cocaine' read as one drug, but crack is SOLVE; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvency is the state of being able to pay one's debts.
